transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-08
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Avery Cole (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Park (PivotLane CTO), Elliot Reed (Lead ML Eng), Jordan Kim (Product)
Recording link: https://redwood.ai/meetings/ff-20261008-pivot-01 (placeholder)

Auto-generated summary (brief, may be imperfect):
PivotLane is evaluating Redwood for an initial PLG/self-serve pilot. Main asks: time-to-first-token (TTFT), free credits to prototype, and whether to start hosted API or commit to Dedicated/Private given latency and data residency constraints. Security questions around SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS. Next step provisioning credits + deeper infra benchmark.

Topics detected: quickstart credits, hosted vs dedicated vs VPC private, latency targets, cost tradeoffs, SOC2 + KMS, rollout timeline

Transcript body:
[00:00] Avery: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um this is Avery from Redwood, i'm the AE working on the PivotLane account, happy to kick off, we've got about 45 mins on the calendar, who wants to intro quickly?
[00:12] Maya: yeah thanks, Maya here, CTO at PivotLane, we run a merchant analytics product, looking to add LLM features for invoice summarization and merchant support. today we've got elliot our ml eng, and jordan product to scope what quickstart might look like.
[00:27] Elliot: hi all, quick note, we care about p95 latency under 300ms for short prompts and p95 under 600 for longer convo flows. also strong need for data controls and audit logs.
[00:38] Jordan: and team is thinking we want to move fast — get something in our beta within 3 weeks if possible — so TTFT is huge for us.
[00:47] Avery: perfect, that's in line with a standard PLG onramp. two quick q's from our side: what infra are you on today (cloud/regions) and what's your expected volume for the first sprints?
[00:59] Maya: we're on AWS us-east-1, running microservices in EKS, and initial traffic is low: maybe 20-200 calls/day per service, but we expect spikes — could go to a few hundred qps in peak tests.
[01:12] Samir: (SE) ok helpful — are you planning to host model data in your VPC or are you okay with Redwood hosted? any regulatory or residency constraints?
[01:23] Maya: no specific residency constraints, but we need separation of customer data and want auditability — SOC2 is a must, plus SSO for our org. if a dedicated environment gives better guarantees for latency we want to consider it.
[01:36] Avery: great, that gives us two paths: self-serve hosted API for fastest TTFT — we can get creds and sample app running in a day — or Dedicated/Private if you need capacity guarantees, lower network hops, and stricter isolation. both are supported.
[01:48] Jordan: what about credits and cost? we have a low budget for the prototype but want representative perf numbers.
[01:54] Avery: we typically provide free credits for PLG trials — for a pilot like this we'd provision a bundle (we discussed 30k tokens as a baseline for similar customers, but we can scale). the credits let you validate correctness and latency at small scale.
[02:07] Elliot: can you explain the latency differences? like hosted vs dedicated — network hop seems obvious but are there other factors?
[02:14] Samir: sure, quick primer — hosted routes go through our public control plane to multi-tenant serving pools, which are highly optimized but have slightly higher variance due to noisy neighbors. dedicated gives you pinned GPU pools, lower tail latency and predictable throughput. private/VPC on-prem removes internet hops but requires more setup. also caching, batching and kernel selection affect token-level latency.
[02:36] Maya: noisy neighbors.. got it. how big of a lift is dedicated to spin up?
[02:41] Avery: for Redwood Dedicated, we can provision a reserved pool — typical lead is 2-4 weeks for a full reserved setup but we do burst/temporary dedicated options for pilots to shorten time. for Private (VPC) a week-to-several-weeks depending on networking and IAM integration.
[02:56] Jordan: hmm 2-4 weeks is long, we need quick feedback into product decisions, so maybe start hosted and then swap to dedicated if tail latency is bad?
[03:05] Samir: that's our common suggestion — start hosted self-serve to prove product/UX and prompt engineering, then upgrade to Dedicated once you have sustained load or need tighter SLOs. we support pinned model variants so your API doesn't break on switch.
[03:19] Elliot: on switching models — do you keep prompts and KV cache compatibility? our users do multi-turn support flows, so warm starts matter.
[03:26] Samir: yes we have KV cache management and support for prefix caching to reduce cold-starts; migration between model variants keeps session continuity at the API layer, though exact warm cache behavior depends on model architecture and quantization. sometimes there's a small transient quality shift.
[03:45] Maya: ok good. can you walk through security: SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs — what do we get out of the box for hosted?
[03:53] Avery: hosted is SOC2 compliant; we provide audit logs, role-based access controls, and SSO via SAML or OIDC. for encryption at rest we integrate with KMS on Dedicated/Private so you can provide keys. for hosted we manage keys but we can add contractual commitments and logging exports.
[04:12] Jordan: are there limitations on PII? we need to avoid customer data being used for model training.
[04:18] Samir: default is no training on customer data — we have data usage opt-out and contractual terms for enterprise. for Private deployments you keep data on prem.
[04:26] Elliot: curious about streaming and function call support — we need streaming responses and structured outputs for our ticket triage flow.
[04:33] Avery: yep streaming and structured outputs are supported in the API; we also have first-class tool/function-calling patterns. we can share a quick sample Node/Python snippet.
[04:43] Jordan: great — we want a quick demo for the product team.
[04:46] Maya: timeline-wise, we want beta in 3 weeks. what's realistic if we go hosted?
[04:51] Avery: hosted — realistic to get devs generating tokens within 1-3 days, an internal beta in 1-2 weeks depending on how much prompt tuning you do. that aligns with your 3-week goal.
[05:02] Samir: to make sure it's smooth, we'll hand you a TTFT checklist: SDK install, API key, a sample prompt set, and a minimal integration checklist for streaming and error handling.
[05:12] Elliot: perfect, can you provide cost estimates for our expected prompt mix? we have short invoice summarization prompts and longer multi-turn support convos.
[05:20] Avery: yes — if you share sample prompt examples and expected call volumes, Samir can run a token-level cost breakdown and a p95 latency estimate for hosted vs dedicated. we also have Optimize suggestions like batching and quantization that reduce token cost.
[05:34] Maya: about observability — do we get per-route latency and token breakdowns in the console?
[05:39] Samir: yes console provides per-route/model dashboards, token-level cost, trace hooks, and error rate breakdowns. for Dedicated/Private we can extend retention windows and export metrics to your monitoring stack.
[05:51] Jordan: any heavy infra pre-reqs for quickstart? VPC peering, firewall rules?
[05:56] Avery: for hosted none. for Private/VPC you'd need some networking and IAM setup; we have a runbook and SE support to help.
[06:04] Elliot: what about performance testing — if we wanted to run a 1k qps load test, can Redwood support a benchmark run and do you provide scripts?
[06:12] Samir: yes we run benchmark harnesses with customers. for high QPS tests we recommend Dedicated reserved pools. we'll share synthetic load scripts, and if you want we can run a joint benchmark with a small dedicated burst.
[06:25] Maya: ok sounds good. quick question: are there any known differences between open model variants on Redwood and the upstream model implementations (tokenization, truncation)?
[06:33] Samir: slight differences can happen due to tokenization libraries and quantization; we publish model profiles and we run evals to verify parity. when we onboard models we include expected tokenization discrepancies in the profile.
[06:45] Jordan: can you share the quickstart guide link?
[06:48] Avery: sure — we'll include that in the follow up. quick reference: https://redwood.ai/docs/quickstart and our security pack: https://redwood.ai/security (placeholders). also the deck we used internally: https://redwood.ai/decks/pivotlane-quickstart.pdf
[07:04] Elliot: i'd like to flag a constraint — our legal wants to see contractual language around data retention and deletion and ability to audit logs.
[07:13] Avery: understood — i'll send our standard security/compliance pack and we can arrange a legal touchpoint. for Private deployments you'll have the strongest guarantees.
[07:22] Maya: circling back to cost — if we go hosted for prototype, and later decide dedicated, how does billing migration work? do we lose credits or have double billing?
[07:32] Avery: credits applied to your account are usable regardless of hosting mode; committed reserved capacity for Dedicated is a separate contract but we can offset credits during transition to avoid double-billing. we'll detail that in the quote.
[07:46] Jordan: are there any sample customers who've done the hosted->dedicated path? might help us convince finance.
[07:52] Avery: yes several—we can share anonymized case studies and a short reference list.
[07:58] (brief cross-talk)
[08:05] Samir: a couple of tactical notes — for TTFT you'll want to: 1) Sign up for API key, 2) install SDK, 3) run a couple of sample prompts, 4) iterate on prompt set and monitor p95. we'll put this into a playbook.
[08:23] Elliot: ok please include a sample Postman collection or curl examples.
[08:27] Avery: will do.
[08:30] Maya: if we want to keep everything in-house later, what does Private look like? timeline/cost?
[08:36] Samir: Private is essentially a customer-managed control plane; deployment can be cloud VPC or on-prem containers. lead time depends on networking and compliance; typical ramp is 2-6 weeks. licensing varies by support tier.
[08:49] Jordan: for our beta i'd prefer hosted — lower friction. security questions can be answered with the pack and the legal review.
[08:55] Maya: agree. one more: do you have SDKs for Go? our backend is in Go.
[08:59] Avery: yes we have official SDKs for Python, Node, Go and some community SDKs. we'll include code snippets.
[09:06] Elliot: can we get a small testbed with a dedicated burst node to replicate tail latency? even a day or two would help.
[09:12] Samir: yes we can provision a short burst dedicated instance for benchmark days. i'll add that to the action items.
[09:19] Jordan: great.
[09:22] (pause)
[09:30] Avery: recap from Redwood side — we'll: send security pack + SOC2 summary, provision 30k credits, share quickstart guide + SDK snippets, Samir will run latency/cost spreadsheet for your prompt mix, and we'll schedule a technical deep dive w/ infra. anything missing?
[09:52] Maya: sounds right. add legal doc review and pricing for switching to Dedicated if needed.
[09:57] Avery: noted.
[10:00] Jordan: can you also add a simple checklist for TTFT for our developers?
[10:04] Samir: yes checklist will be in the follow-up email.
[10:08] Elliot: last nit — do you support customer-managed KMS for hosted?
[10:12] Samir: hosted uses our managed keys but we offer bring-your-own-key (BYOK) on Dedicated and Private. for hosted we can discuss contractual encryption assurances.
[10:24] Maya: ok that will probably be fine for prototype.
[10:27] Avery: perfect. i'll send minutes and a link to all shared artifacts. thanks everyone, any closing thoughts?
[10:33] Jordan: no, thanks all. excited to try it.
[10:36] Maya: thanks, talk soon.
[10:40] Avery: bye all.

Meeting end.
